# Salary Cap Fantasy Football Constitution — 2025 Edition

> This document is open to edits even during the season pending a vote. A rule change requires a vote from **6 owners**. For all salary cap purposes, money is rounded to the nearest dollar.

## I. General Rules

### A. Rosters
1. Weekly rosters consist of standard fantasy football positions: **1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 TE, 1 RB/WR/TE, 1 K, 1 DEF**, plus **10 bench spots**.
2. Each team is given **2 Injured Reserve** spots.

### B. Scoring
1. **Standard Half PPR** scoring is used week-to-week.
2. The competition format is **head-to-head**.

### C. Regular Season
The regular season runs from **Week 1 through Week 18**.

### D. Tanking Prevention
If an owner plays a player who is on bye or injured (well in advance of game time), the penalty will be:
1. **1st offense** — Warning
2. **2nd offense** — Forfeits 3rd round pick

## II. Initial Draft
A. The initial league draft uses standard auction format with **$300** as the starting amount per team.
B. The amount the winning owner pays for a player becomes that player's year-one salary. After the draft, owners have until the regular season kicks off to determine the contract length for each drafted player.

## III. In-Season Free Agency
A. Once the draft has concluded, each team receives **$300 in salary cap space**, minus the amount spent during the draft.
B. Owners may then use this money to bid for free agents during the season.
C. Bidding uses Yahoo's **FAB system**, with weekly rolling reverse-standings tie breakers. Bidding ends at **11:59 PT Tuesday**. After that, players may be added for $0.
D. Teams may not spend additional money if they are already at or above the salary cap for the current season.
   1. This rule does not apply to signing league-minimum ($0) deals.
E. The minimum salary for a player is **$0**.
   1. If a team owner reaches the salary cap ceiling, they may only sign additional players to $0 deals.
F. All in-season signings are **one-year deals**.

### G. Cuts
1. Owners may cut any player at any time.
2. **Players signed to a one-year deal:**
   a. Become free agents that any team may bid on.
   b. The player's old contract still counts against the cap for the remainder of the year.
3. **Players with multiple years remaining on their contract:**
   a. Become free agents that any team may bid on.
   b. The cut player's salary counts against the team that cut him for the full amount of his salary the remainder of the year.
   c. Following years count as: **75% of year 2, 50% of year 3, 25% of year 4**.
4. If a player retires (defined as a Google search for "Player X retire" returning articles evidencing retirement), that player's entire salary is removed immediately.

## IV. Trading
A. The **trade deadline** is at the conclusion of **Week 14**.
B. If the trade involves a player with a salary over **$20**, the combined salaries of players exchanged from each team must be within **±25% of the higher salary**.
   - *Legal:* Team A = $75 and Team B = $100.
   - *Illegal:* Team A = $75 and Team B = $124.

### C. Salary Cap Space in Trades
1. **Salary Compensation** — used to bring exchanged player salaries within 125% of each other.
   - *Example:* Team A = $75, Team B = $125. Team A includes $20 of salary → legal.
2. **Salary Considerations** — used to improve an offer.
   a. Not required to stay within 125%.
      - *Example:* Team A = $75, Team B = $100. Team B includes $25 → legal.
   b. May have performance-based criteria when agreed upon by both owners.
      - *Example:* $25 sent from A to B if Player A plays 16 games next year.
   c. Traded salary must first cover the trade cost, then any negative cap space, before being usable in free agency.
      - *Example:* Team A receives $10 but is $9 over the cap → only $1 available.
3. **Future Rookie Draft Picks** may also be exchanged.
   a. Picks do not have to fall within 125%.
   b. Picks may have performance-based criteria attached to the round.
   c. Picks can be traded **up to 3 years** into the future (any pick viewable on the team's roster).

D. Trades do not need to include a player. Cap and picks alone may be the items exchanged.
   - *Example:* Team A sends $35 to Team B for a 2nd round pick.

## V. Playoffs
A. The league playoffs run during the **NFL playoffs**.
B. Team rosters and salary caps are locked once **Week 18** ends. Owners enter the offseason with these rosters.
C. The **top 4 teams** in the regular season standings advance to the playoffs.
   1. Ties: most points scored, then head-to-head wins.

### D. Playoff Format
1. Player contracts are not considered during the playoffs.
2. The four teams field a lineup of regular starters only — **no bench**.
   a. No lineup changes after playoffs start, except for injury (owner receives the injured player's back-up).
   b. If a player is eliminated from the NFL playoffs, he cannot earn additional points the rest of the postseason.
3. Each owner first chooses any of his own regular-season players to retain for the playoff roster.
4. A draft of all remaining players (including those from non-playoff teams) follows.
   - **Straight draft** in seed order; the regular-season champion holds the first pick.
5. The playoffs are played **rotisserie style**.
   a. The team with the most points after the Super Bowl is crowned champion.

## VI. Offseason Free Agency
A. The offseason begins the **Monday after the Super Bowl** each year.
B. There is **no maximum contract** for free agents.
C. A free agent may be offered a deal of **1 to 4 years**.
   1. Future-year salary follows:
      a. **Year 2:** 105% of year-1, or $1, whichever is greater
      b. **Year 3:** 110% of year-2, or $1, whichever is greater
      c. **Year 4:** 115% of year-3, or $1, whichever is greater

### D. Designations for Expiring Contracts
Owners of players with expiring contracts may designate **two** as Restricted Free Agent Offer, **one** as Franchise Tag, and **one** as Mid-Level Extension.
   a. Designations cannot be used on players who were not on the owner's roster at the end of the regular season.

#### Restricted Free Agency
2. RFA salary starts at **110% of the player's previous-season salary**.
   a. Other owners silently bid on each player separately. The previous owner may match the best offer to retain; otherwise the new owner is awarded the player.
      i. Owners may not bid more than their available cap space. Acquired/retained RFA players may be signed 1–4 years.
      ii. Original owners may match a bid that puts them over the cap, but doing so ends their offseason — they cannot add anyone else until **after** the free agent draft.
   b. RFA runs **one player at a time** in the order of ESPN's fantasy rankings on the day the period begins.
   c. Other owners have **48 hours** to bid once a player is up.
   d. The restricting team has **24 hours** to decide whether to match.

#### Franchise Tag
3. Franchise-tagged players are paid the average salary of the **top 5 highest paid players at that position**.
   a. One-year contract only.
   b. Cannot be used on the same player in consecutive seasons (regardless of trades).
4. May not be used if it puts the team over the cap.

#### Mid-Level Extension
5. The Mid-Level Extension is a **3-year contract** structured as **$15 / $30 / $45** (regardless of position).
6. May only be used on a player that:
   a. Is **not coming off a rookie draft contract** (e.g., Justin Jefferson entering year 5 is ineligible; Tank Dell entering year 2 is eligible since he wasn't drafted in the rookie draft).
   b. Had a previous-season salary **less than $10**.
7. May not be used if it puts the team over the cap.

### E. Unrestricted Free Agency
1. Takes place at an agreed-upon date.
2. Any players not under contract are eligible.
3. Held online during one **live draft**.
4. In random order, owners nominate players for bidding.
   a. Owners have **30 seconds** to place bids. Bids are for the year-1 salary amount.
   b. Highest bid wins the player.
5. After the draft, owners have until the start of the season to decide contract lengths (1–4 years) for newly acquired players.

### F. Rookie Draft
1. Held each offseason at an agreed-upon date.
2. Consists of **incoming NFL rookies only**.
3. Order is the **reverse of the previous year's standings**.
   a. **Straight draft** (not snake).
4. The rookie draft is **3 rounds**.
5. Rookie contracts:
   a. **1st Round:** $5 · **2nd Round:** $3 · **3rd Round:** $1
   b. Rookies may be signed up to 4 years after being drafted. Owners have until Week 1 of the regular season to determine rookie contract lengths.
      i. Rookie deals **increase $1 per year**.
      ii. If a rookie is cut, normal cut rules apply.

### G. Fees and Pay-Outs
1. League entry fee: **$100/year**.
2. Payout structure:
   - **Regular Season:** 1st — $400 · 2nd — $200 · 3rd — $100
   - **Playoffs:** 1st — $200 · 2nd — $100
